questions.question: How does petabase-scale mining of RdRP fragments reveal geographically concentrated yet taxonomically unassigned RNA virus diversity that falls below 40% identity to curated references?
questions.rationale: Across 53 fragments, 86.8% align below 40% identity and a plurality (10/53) only map to unclassified RdRP profiles, indicating a persistent reference gap. Three quarters (24/32) of candidate clusters flag as novel, with low-identity clusters distributed across arthropod transcriptomes, plant metatranscriptomes, and aquatic viromes, particularly from North America and metadata-poor runs. Given the upstream screen spans ~5.7M runs and 131k candidate novel sOTUs, these signals imply that viral polymerase novelty concentrates in specific sources and regions that curated databases do not yet cover.
questions.expected_test: Intersect run-level sources and regions with RdRP alignment identity and sOTU novelty flags to quantify which sampling contexts drive the <40% identity fraction.
